Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1220 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Valid 311200Z - 011200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
MISSOURI INTO FAR NORTHERN ARKANSAS...

...SUMMARY...
Scattered strong to severe storms appear possible from Iowa
southward into the Ozark Plateau, and over the central and southern
High Plains Friday afternoon and evening. Sporadic occurrences of
damaging wind and large hail will be the primary hazards, with a
conditional risk for a few tornadoes over Missouri.

...Southern IA into MO and northern AR...
A zone of severe potential remains evident on Friday from southeast
IA across much of MO and into northern AR, though complicating
factors remain.

A shortwave trough will move southeastward toward the lower MO and
mid MS Valleys, which will enhance mid and upper level winds.
However, temperatures aloft will not cool much, and as such,
midlevel lapse rates will remain relatively poor. In addition, early
day storms are expected, and at least some degree of temporary
stabilization may occur, especially if an MCS develops over NE/KS
Thursday night as depicted by some models. 

That said, low-level moisture will likely either remain intact or
redevelop as any residual outflows modify. Daytime heating and 70s F
dewpoints will still result in MLCAPE of 2000-3000 J/kg just ahead
of the cold front which will extend from the IA/MO border area
southwestward into northwest AR by 00Z. 

Southwest 850 mb winds will maintain warm advection toward the MS
Valley, and this is also where low-level SRH will be greatest. Given
decent model agreement with redevelopment late in the day along the
cold front, a small Slight Risk has been introduced, covering
damaging wind and conditional tornado potential.

...Eastern CO and NM...
Mid to upper-level northwesterly winds may increase a bit on Friday
as a shortwave trough moves southeastward across the central Plains,
with 20-25 kt speeds at 500 mb expected. Minor cooling aloft may
occur across the High Plains as this wave glances the area.

Surface winds will veer to northeasterly by late afternoon,
maintaining moisture and enhancing upslope flow. Storms are likely
to form over the higher terrain of southeast CO into much of
northeast NM, with mean winds supporting southeastward storm
motions. It appears enough storm coverage may develop to support
locally severe outflow winds through early evening.

..Jewell.. 07/30/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0217 PM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Valid 011200Z - 021200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
THE OHIO AND TENNESSEE VALLEYS...AND OVER MUCH OF NEW MEXICO...

...SUMMARY...
Scattered storms, some severe, will be possible across portions of
the Ohio and Tennessee Valleys into the Central Gulf Coast states,
and over parts of central and eastern New Mexico Saturday afternoon
and evening.

...OH Valley southward into MS and AL...
A shortwave trough will move from the mid MS Valley southeastward
into the OH and TN Valleys on Saturday, with modest 25-30 kt
midlevel southwesterlies developing ahead of it. At the surface, low
pressure will move across southern IL and IN during the day, with a
cold front extending southwestward across the lower MS Valley by
late afternoon. A very moist air mass will exist ahead of the cold
front, with 70s F dewpoints.

Areas of early rain/storms are likely to be ongoing within the warm
advection zone east of the low over IN/KY/TN, but southwest surface
winds and heating will result in moderate instability redeveloping
ahead of the cold front with MLCAPE averaging 2000-2500 J/kg. The
front will easily support scattered storms by mid afternoon from IN
southward into MS/AL. Marginal deep-layer shear combined with
substantial moisture content should yield corridors of mixed-mode
storms capable of damaging gusts and perhaps isolated marginal hail.
A weak tornado or two cannot be ruled out where low-level winds are
backed within the very moist/low-LCL environment, but overall it
appears these would be brief.

...Much of eastern NM...
Winds aloft will adjust to more of a northerly direction on
Saturday, with a cold front plunging south into TX. Western portions
of this front will extend into eastern NM, where 50s F dewpoints
will remain, along with easterly surface winds.

Midlevel lapse rates will be relatively steep, with the northerly
flow regime resulting in around 40 kt deep-layer effective shear.
This combination should support a few severe storms capable of hail
or damaging gusts as storms develop over the higher terrain and move
generally southward through the evening.

..Jewell.. 07/30/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0335 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Valid 021200Z - 071200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Days 4 and 5/Sunday and Monday...

The models remain in relatively good agreement in depicting a strong
short-wave trough and attending belt of mid-level flow progressing
along the international border from the northern Rockies into the
northern Plains. Meanwhile, an associated cold front is forecast to
move into the northern High Plains on Sunday and the upper MS Valley
into northern Plains on Monday. Low-level ridging from the Great
Lakes into Ozark Plateau may disrupt the advection of a maritime
tropical air mass ahead of the front. However, evapotranspiration
will contribute to pockets of higher moisture content, which,
combined with the eastern extension of an EML plume, will contribute
to moderate instability ahead of a surface cold front both
afternoons.

On Sunday, the strongest forcing for ascent associated with a lead 
vorticity lobe is expected to remain across SK and MB with capping
to the south of that feature potentially limiting storm coverage
along the front in ND. On the condition that storms develop, the
presence of moderate instability and 30-40 kt of deep-layer shear
would support storm organization and at least an isolated severe
weather threat. Additional severe storms appear possible from the
Mid-Atlantic into Southeast ahead of a short-wave trough moving
through the Great Lakes, OH Valley, and Gulf Coast states.  

On Monday, a secondary disturbance and associated jet streak are
forecast to move into the northern Plains, supporting a potentially
greater severe weather threat from the northern Plains into the
upper MS Valley. 


...Days 6 through 8/Tuesday through Thursday...

The 00Z deterministic and ensemble mean solutions indicate
low-amplitude troughing across the north-central states on Tuesday
with a belt of enhanced mid-level flow extending from the northern
Rockies into the upper Great Lakes. A few severe storms appear
possible over the central High Plains where the southern periphery
of the stronger mid-level flow is juxtaposed with a moist and
unstable upslope regime. 

By Wednesday and Thursday, the ensemble mean solutions indicate a
modestly enhanced belt of quasi-zonal flow across the northern tier
of the CONUS. However, there is considerable spread across the
deterministic models with the location and track of disturbances
embedded within that air stream. As such, confidence in the location
and extent of any severe weather threat is low.

..Mead.. 07/30/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1227 AM CDT Fri Jul 31 2026

Valid 311200Z - 011200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE OZARKS AND MID MISSISSIPPI VALLEY...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts and hail will be possible this
afternoon and evening across parts of the Ozarks and mid Mississippi
Valley. Isolated severe gusts will also be possible in parts of the
southern Plains and from east-central Colorado into northeastern New
Mexico.

...Ozarks/Mid Mississippi Valley...
At mid-levels, a positively tilted shortwave trough will move
southeastward across the mid to upper Mississippi Valley. An
associated cold front will advance southeastward into the western
Ozarks. Ahead of the front, an axis of moisture will be in place
with surface dewpoints in the 70s F. As surface temperatures warm,
moderate instability will develop along and near the moist axis,
with MLCAPE forecast to peak in the 2500 to 3500 J/kg range during
the afternoon. In addition to the instability, mid-level flow will
be westerly at 30 to 35 knots, which will contribute to moderate
deep-layer shear over much of the moist sector. This will result a
mixed mode with supercells and organized line segments both
possible. Along the instability axis, 0-3 km lapse rates are
forecast to peak near 7 C/km which will support a threat for severe
wind gusts. The threat could persist into the early to mid evening
as storms move southeastward across the mid Mississippi Valley.

...Southern Plains/East-central Colorado/Northeast New Mexico...
Northwesterly mid-level flow will be in place across much of the
central U.S. today. At the surface, a cold front will move southward
into central Oklahoma and the Texas Panhandle by afternoon. An axis
of moderate instability will develop ahead of the front as
temperatures become hot in the mid to late afternoon. Increasing
low-level convergence near the front will result in scattered
thunderstorm development. These storms will move south-southeastward
across the Red River Valley and southward across the Caprock of west
Texas. Very steep low to mid-level lapse rates and large temperature
dewpoint spreads exceeding 40 degrees F in some areas will result in
a potential for isolated severe wind gusts.

Further west into east-central Colorado and northeast New Mexico, an
axis of instability will develop by afternoon in and near the
foothills of the southern Rockies. Storms will form in the mid to
late afternoon in the higher terrain and gradually move
southeastward into the lower elevations. Steep low to mid-level
lapse rates will support a potential for isolated severe gusts. Hail
could also occur with the stronger updrafts.

..Broyles/Chalmers.. 07/31/2026
